subject: How to prevent '1.00' values overlapping with residuals of observed (manifest) variables when using semPaths 'lisrel' style?

messages.author: 42a8db694a549d17
messages.subject: How to prevent '1.00' values overlapping with residuals of observed (manifest) variables when using semPaths 'lisrel' style?
parts:
Hello all,

After fitting a CFA model in lavaan I'm now plotting the results using semPaths. However, when I use 'style = "lisrel"' (single-headed straight arrows), the residuals of the observed variables are obscured by overlapping '1.00' values (see attached image). I don't have this issue if I use the default style (double-headed curved arrows; see same image). Does anyone know how to prevent this so the values are presented clearly? Any advice is greatly appreciated.

Many thanks,
Mary

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: How to prevent '1.00' values overlapping with residuals of observed (manifest) variables when using semPaths 'lisrel' style?
parts:
Dear Mary,

May you post the call to semPaths() you used so we can learn more about the settings used? I did a test using the example of lavaan::cfa() and did not have this problem.

library(lavaan)
library(semPlot)
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)
semPaths(fit, what = "est", style = "lisrel")

fit2<- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, meanstructure = TRUE)
semPaths(fit2,what = "est", style = "lisrel")

Maybe something related to other settings used?

-- Shu Fai
